title: KV rollout capacity simulation Q1 2026
body:
Purpose:
This sheet simulates the GPU capacity and regional impact of onboarding two new model variants (prod: redwood-rx-70b-quant, fallback: rx-13b-int8) with a prefix/KV cache usage pattern. The goal is to estimate node/GPU scaling, memory pressure from KV cache, and regional capacity risks across three rollout scenarios (expected, conservative, pessimistic).

Assumptions and constants used in the simulation:
- Models: redwood-rx-70b-quant (primary), redwood-rx-13b-int8 (fallback)
- Target rollout traffic: phased ramp to +18% global QPS over baseline in 8 weeks
- Average request length (tokens in generation): 160 tokens
- Average prompt length: 80 tokens
- KV cache used for repeating conversation prefixes: cache hit rate modeled at 35% overall; 60% for top-10 heavy users
- KV entry per turn: average 1.8 entries per session (embedding of chunked prefixes + attention state pointers)
- Average KV entry serialized size: 2.1 KB (70B quantization-friendly entries smaller than float32 but include metadata)
- Working set eviction window: 48 hours for active users, cold storage for >48h
- Node types and memory: p4d (8xA100 40GB) logical grouping, p4d-equivalent GPU memory per GPU 40GB; p5-large (80GB) for private clouds noted but not used in baseline
- Baseline global GPU pool: 3 regions (us-west1, eu-west1, ap-southeast1), totals: 1,920 GPUs (split 50/35/15 by region)
- Current baseline utilization (token-serving): 62% avg (by GPU)

Sheet: KV cache footprint and GPU memory pressure table (per-region aggregated)

| Region | GPUs (baseline) | Baseline util (%) | Additional QPS (est) | Avg KV entries active | KV bytes per GPU (est) | KV mem % of GPU RAM | Memory headroom left (GB) | Nodes to add (expected) | Notes |
| ------ | ---------------:| ----------------:| -------------------:| ---------------------:| ---------------------:| --------------------:| ------------------------:| ----------------------:| ----- |
| us-west1 | 960 | 65 | +9% (peak +14%) | 2.9M | 6.09 GB | 15.2% | 34.8 GB | +12 GPUs (~1.5 nodes) | heavy traffic from NA customers; caching benefits highest |
| eu-west1 | 672 | 60 | +5.6% (peak +9%) | 1.85M | 3.89 GB | 9.7% | 36.1 GB | +6 GPUs (~0.8 nodes) | predictable batch traffic, good headroom |
| ap-southeast1 | 288 | 58 | +3.4% (peak +6%) | 0.95M | 2.02 GB | 5.1% | 37.98 GB | +4 GPUs (~0.5 nodes) | bursty; risk window during regional promotions |

Notes on calculations: 
- Avg KV entries active = (estimated active sessions * avg KV entries). Active sessions approximated from QPS * session_length model (session length = 6 requests).
- KV bytes per GPU = (total active KV entries across region * 2.1 KB) / GPUs. Includes replication/overhead factor 1.1 for metadata and compression inefficiencies.
- KV mem % of GPU RAM uses 40GB per GPU baseline.

Model tokenization and per-token memory footprint notes:
- For 70B quant variant, KV architectural pointers and checkpoint references lead to slightly higher per-entry metadata (estimated +15% vs 13B). We already baked +10% in the 2.1 KB estimate for safety.
- Where KV memory approaches >25% of GPU RAM we flag for placement to p5-large pools or dedicated cache nodes. See placement guidance section.

Scenario summary (expected / conservative / pessimistic):
- Expected: ramp to +18% QPS; cache hit 35%; global additional GPUs needed: +22 GPUs (spread: 12 us-west, 6 eu-west, 4 ap-southeast). Estimated infra spend growth: ~+9% monthly.
- Conservative (higher growth & lower caching): ramp to +26% QPS; cache hit 20%; additional GPUs: +46 GPUs (safety buffer) — consider committed capacity; infra spend growth: +18% monthly.
- Pessimistic (peak concentrated +40% regional spike): burst +40% QPS localized to us-west, cache hit 15%; additional GPUs: +78 GPUs needed short-term in us-west (use burst capacity / cross-region routing).

Regional mitigation recommendations:
- us-west1: pre-warm an extra 16 GPUs in week 2 of rollout; enable cross-region spillover to eu-west1 for non-PII routes; enable model variant fallback to rx-13b-int8 for tail-latency sensitive routes to reduce memory pressure.
- eu-west1: no immediate expansion required for expected scenario; schedule +8 GPU reserve if conservative triggers.
- ap-southeast1: leverage burst pool; ensure autoscaling policies allow 2 node scale in within 90s for padding during marketing spikes.

Operational checklist before traffic ramp:
- [ ] Add KV telemetry probes to trace per-GPU KV footprint by tenant and route (JIRA-OPS-9876).
- [ ] Implement soft-limits on per-tenant KV allocation with backpressure signal to SDK (engineering PR referenced).
- [ ] Create canary routing rule that sends 3% of traffic to rx-70b-quant in us-west then gradually increase to 30% over 4 weeks if error/latency/kv-growth within thresholds.
- [ ] Run synthetic load test matching 140 token avg generation for 2 hours to validate eviction policy and per-GPU memory above assumptions.

Open questions / risks captured:
- Risk: KV entry estimate distribution may be skewed by a small set of enterprise customers; need tenant-level cap enforcement to avoid noisy-neighbor deaths.
- Question: If quantized model memory usage increases (kernel change), KV overhead could double for 70B variants. Need a guardrail to pin a subset of production traffic to 13B fallback if that happens.

Appendix: example calculation excerpt (us-west1, expected scenario)
- Baseline GPUs: 960; baseline utilization 65% = 624 GPUs effectively busy average.
- Expected additional QPS +9% => approximate extra GPU demand = 0.09 * 624 = 56.2 GPU-equivalents in peak windows (token processing).
- KV active entries estimate: active sessions = QPS * session_length (6) => if region baseline qps 12k, extra qps 1.08k => extra active sessions 6.48k; new concurrent KV entries ~6.48k * 1.8 = 11.66k entries => 11.66k * 2.1 KB * 1.1 overhead = ~26.9 MB extra across region per additional QPS slice. Scale to global and divide by 960 GPUs => ~6.09 GB per GPU increase in total region KV working set (matching table).

Short-form recommendations to product and release engineering:
- Product: include rollout control flags per-route to enable fast rollback to 13B variant and to toggle KV aggressive eviction on a per-customer basis.
- Release eng: block rollout for customers who have sustained >50% long-session traffic unless tenant-level caps exist.

Last checked: metrics snapshot (2026-02-03): global QPS 1.82M/day; avg token length 145; current global hot-pool KV working set ~11.2 TB (replicated), memory utilization per GPU 62%.

Contact: Aisha Kapoor (infra capacity lead) — for follow-ups and model-specific simulation adjustments.

Document history: draft created 2026-01-11; initial simulations added 2026-01-22 by Ethan Mills; canary policy notes added 2026-02-04 by María Torres.
